clue.text: Distracting florid gentleman in German capital of Finnish origin

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun phrase: a red herring is a distracting lead

parts.note: a florid complexion is red
Herr is the German for Mr, a gentleman
taken as written
the capital, or first letter, of German
surface padding with no letters to give in this parse

explanation.surface: A flamboyant gentleman of Finnish descent living in Germany's capital is causing a distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: RED + HERR + IN + G gives RED HERRING. The closing words 'of Finnish origin' have no clear job in this parse; they may hint that herring come from Baltic waters.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading clue that draws attention away from the truth, so it is something distracting.

clue.text: A rise in fraud

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slope joining two levels
second meaning: British slang for a swindle

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a ramp is a racket or swindle, especially one that pushes prices up.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is an inclined surface that rises, and in slang a dishonest scheme or swindle.

clue.text: A Wenceslas footprint

parts.note: surface reading: the good king of the Christmas carol
setter's reading: the carol tells of the page treading in the marks his master's feet left in the snow

explanation.walkthrough: The carol 'Good King Wenceslas' has the line 'In his master's steps he trod, where the snow lay dinted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dint is a hollow or impression left by a blow or pressure, like a footmark in snow.

clue.text: Milton's sweet nymph doing the plumbing

parts.note: in Milton's masque Comus the Lady sings 'Sweet Echo, sweetest nymph'
to sound is to do, in the sense of carrying out a depth measurement; doing the sounding

explanation.surface: Milton's lovely nymph turns her hand to fixing the pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plumbing' suggests pipes and taps; it means measuring the depth of water with a plumb line. Echo is the mountain nymph of Greek myth whom Milton invokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo sounding measures water depth by timing a sound pulse's return, the modern way of plumbing the sea.

clue.text: Early to get a step up?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who gets up early, an early bird
second meaning: the vertical part of a stair

explanation.walkthrough: The 'up' serves both halves: an early riser gets up early, and a riser is the upright face of each step.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is a person who gets out of bed, and also the vertical board between two treads of a staircase.

clue.text: Weapon against the bee?

parts.note: surface reading: something to fend off a stinging insect
setter's reading: a sewing bee is a needlework gathering, so its weapon would fire needles

explanation.walkthrough: A bee is also a social gathering for work, such as a sewing bee; the needle gun was a 19th-century Prussian rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: The needle gun was a breech-loading rifle whose long firing pin, the needle, struck the cartridge's primer.

clue.text: Is under an obligation: do some needlework, love, in return

indicators.note: something given in return goes back the other way, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: to sew is to do needlework
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone in debt takes up sewing for a loved one as repayment.
explanation.walkthrough: SEW and O run backwards make OWES.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe is to be bound to pay or repay something, so 'is under an obligation' is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Honest feller

parts.note: surface reading: a truthful chap
setter's reading: one who fells a tree, as in the story of the boy who chopped the cherry tree and could not tell a lie

explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' looks like slang for fellow; it is one who fells. The legend has young George Washington confessing to his father that he cut down the cherry tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington is the American president of the cherry-tree legend, famed for honesty about chopping it down.

clue.text: She defines effect on her work of a wearer growing stouter

definitions.text: She defines effect on her work of a wearer growing stouter

parts.note: surface reading: a woman giving a definition

parts.words: on her work of a wearer growing stouter
parts.note: setter's reading: a fattening wearer puts strain on the joins of her garments, and her title spells out that strain

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into SEAM and STRESS: her very name describes what a stouter wearer does to her stitching.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress is a woman who sews for a living, and her name literally reads as seam stress.

clue.text: Old town lost God in becoming industrial city

indicators.note: something lost is no longer there, so these letters drop out of the longer name

parts.note: Godmanchester is an ancient town in Cambridgeshire, once a Roman settlement
taken as written; these are the letters removed

explanation.surface: An old town gave up its faith on the way to becoming a modern industrial city.
explanation.walkthrough: Godmanchester is a small English town near Huntingdon; dropping its first three letters leaves MANCHESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester was the great cotton-milling city of the Industrial Revolution in north-west England.

clue.text: The Great North Road's taking a turn east

indicators.note: a turn sends things round the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the Great North Road is the A1, with the 1 read as I, plus the S of the possessive
taken as written

explanation.surface: Britain's main road north suddenly bends off towards the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the Great North Road from London to Edinburgh. AIS plus A is AISA, which read backwards gives ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the East, the Orient, as seen from Europe, so 'east' stands for the continent.

clue.text: Rare peak of performance

parts.note: surface reading: an unusual high point in someone's career
setter's reading: the air is rarefied at this summit, and climbing it is the ultimate achievement

explanation.walkthrough: Rare here hints at thin, rarefied air at extreme altitude; the summit had been reached only twenty years before this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Everest is the world's highest mountain, so it is the peak, and scaling it is the pinnacle of achievement.

clue.text: Ghostly RAF personnel, their goal achieved?

definitions.text: Ghostly RAF personnel, their goal achieved?

parts.note: surface reading: phantom airmen haunting an airfield
setter's reading: the RAF motto 'Per ardua ad astra' aims at the stars, so airmen who arrived would be heavenly bodies

explanation.surface: Ghostly airmen of the Royal Air Force who have finally reached their objective.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF motto means 'through adversity to the stars'. An astral body is the ghostly double of a person, and astral also means starry.
explanation.definitionFit: In occult belief an astral body is a spectral counterpart of the physical body, so it is literally ghostly.

clue.text: Old clothes men with a breezy manner

definitions.text: Old clothes men with a breezy manner

parts.note: surface reading: rag-and-bone dealers who trade in cast-offs
setter's reading: figures dressed in cast-offs stand in fields with the wind flapping their sleeves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old clothes men' suggests second-hand dealers; these figures merely wear the old clothes, out in the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarecrows are figures dressed in discarded clothing and set in fields to frighten birds away.

clue.text: Second item on menu for embattled royal arms supporters

definitions.text: Second item on menu for embattled royal arms supporters

parts.note: surface reading: the next course at a banquet
setter's reading: the nursery rhyme of the warring lion and unicorn lists what they were fed, white first and then the other loaf

explanation.walkthrough: The lion and unicorn support the royal coat of arms; the rhyme says 'Some gave them white bread, and some gave them brown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown bread is wholemeal bread, the second food named in the rhyme about the fighting lion and unicorn.

clue.text: Vehicle none are making use of — just as well, after this!

definitions.text: Vehicle none are making use of — just as well, after this!

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
none is nought, the letter O
making use of something is using it

explanation.surface: A car nobody is driving, and a good thing too after this.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'just as well, after this!' makes the whole clue the definition: after a night's drinking, nobody should be at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousing is drinking and making merry, after which leaving the car alone is the sensible course.

clue.text: Mouse I put to confusion — how dashing!

indicators.note: things brought to confusion are jumbled up, so the preceding letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: I scattered a mouse in a panic — what a dashing feat!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' reads as part of the instruction, but its letters belong in the mix with MOUSE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetuous means rushing headlong without thought, as dashing does when it describes a reckless charge.

clue.text: Current turn concerning "mother's ruin"

indicators.note: turn means go round the other way, so the letters that follow are read backwards

parts.note: re is Latin for 'concerning', as in a letter heading
mother's ruin is an old nickname for gin

explanation.surface: A sudden turn in the debate about gin's evils.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus GIN reversed gives NIGER. 'Current' looks like a noun for electricity or a trend; here it is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a current of water, and the Niger is the great river of West Africa.

clue.text: Wo-back in debt! But went on in liquidation

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters go into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: being in debt is being in the red

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written, a carter's call to a horse

explanation.surface: A cry of alarm at being in debt, yet the business carried on in liquidation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquidation' looks like a bankrupt firm; it means simply going on liquid, water. Wo is the old call to halt a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To row is to propel a boat across water, so having rowed is having gone on over the liquid.

clue.text: Think to change a sou? That's no light matter -

parts.note: to ponder is to think

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a sou is an old French coin of small value

explanation.surface: Weighing up whether to exchange a small coin is a grave matter.
explanation.walkthrough: PONDER followed by SOU rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponderous means heavy and weighty, the opposite of light, so it describes something that is no light matter.

clue.text: Opposition to his handiwork there may be, even if shadowy

definitions.text: Opposition to his handiwork there may be, even if shadowy

parts.words: Opposition to his handiwork there may be
parts.note: surface reading: a craftsman whose work meets resistance
setter's reading: the Opposition party has a shadow cabinet, so there is an opposing version of what this joiner builds

explanation.surface: A craftsman whose work attracts opponents, even if they lurk in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the Opposition forms a shadow cabinet to face the government's cabinet; the clue treats a cabinet as furniture built by a joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinetmaker is a skilled joiner who builds fine furniture such as cupboards and cabinets.

clue.text: Ancestor from the Hook?

parts.note: surface reading: a forebear from the Hook of Holland
setter's reading: the Germanic tribe came from a hook-shaped region, and their name also means a fish-hook

explanation.walkthrough: The Angles, ancestors of the English, came from Angeln, a hook-shaped district of Schleswig; angle is also an old word for a fish-hook.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angle is a member of the Germanic people who settled England, so one of the nation's forebears.

clue.text: Thomson's prentice potter?

parts.note: surface reading: an apprentice in someone's pottery
setter's reading: the poet James Thomson wrote of teaching a young learner how to shoot, and to pot is to shoot

explanation.walkthrough: Thomson's 'The Seasons' has 'Delightful task! to rear the tender thought, To teach the young idea how to shoot'. A pot-shot is a casual shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In Thomson's line the young idea is the learner being taught to shoot, an apprentice marksman.

clue.text: O Mrs Othello, the devil a conclusion you came to after all that poetry

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what you came to is where you stop, so the rest of the name is cut away

parts.note: Desdemona is Othello's wife in Shakespeare
a demon is a devil; these letters are removed

indicators.note: 'conclusion' keeps only the first letter of 'a'

parts.note: the closing letter of the name, also removed

explanation.surface: An apostrophe to Othello's wife, cursing the conclusion reached after so much verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the devil and the closing letter from Othello's wife's name leaves three letters to follow O. The parse is loose; the definition at the end is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, so a collection of them is a body of poetry.

clue.text: Jumper done?

parts.note: surface reading: a knitted woollen garment
setter's reading: the word for where a jumper goes across a fence also means finished

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like asking whether the knitting is finished; the answer is what a jumper goes, which also means finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means finished or ended, and it is also the direction of a jump across an obstacle.

clue.text: Shrewdly dolichocephalic

definitions.note: an adverb where the answer is an adjective, meaning shrewd
definitions.meaning: first meaning: shrewd, far-sighted and wise
second meaning: the anthropologist's term for having a long skull

explanation.walkthrough: The plain sense is long in the head; the figurative sense is shrewd. The clue's adverb is loose for an adjectival answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolichocephalic literally means having a long skull, and long-headed figuratively means sagacious or canny.

clue.text: Splashdown — when terminated

parts.note: surface reading: a space capsule landing at sea
setter's reading: a splash poured down into a drink until the drinker says 'when' to stop it

explanation.walkthrough: In 1973 splashdown meant the end of an Apollo mission; here it is a splash of mixer poured into whisky until someone says 'say when'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is the classic splash added to spirits, poured until the drinker calls 'when'.

clue.text: Can't do without them

parts.note: surface reading: someone unable to manage a task
setter's reading: the things one cannot manage without are the indispensable ones

explanation.walkthrough: A plain description of the answer, with little disguise beyond its offhand tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentials are necessities, the things that are indispensable and cannot be dispensed with.
